author: Claude
message:
Defect B: refit RANSAC plane on inliers, fix acceptance and sampling

plane_ransac returned the plane defined by the 3 randomly sampled seed
points instead of refitting to all inliers, so the floor reference was
set by 3 noisy pixels rather than the ~90k that agree with it. On
synthetic tilted-floor data this refit lowers floor RMS error ~4x
(3.7mm -> 0.8mm).

Also in the same function:
- np.random.choice used replace=True, which can draw the same point
  three times and produce a degenerate plane; use replace=False.
- best_plane was unbound when no iteration passed the acceptance gate,
  raising UnboundLocalError; initialize it and raise a readable error.
- acceptance required both more inliers AND lower mean distance over ALL
  points, which can reject a strictly better plane; score on inlier
  count and break ties on mean inlier distance.

Adds plane_fit_lstsq (SVD total-least-squares plane fit) for the refit.

author: Claude
message:
Defect C: treat depth dropouts as missing in background estimate

get_bground_im_file computed the background with np.nanmedian, but
invalid depth pixels are 0, not NaN, so zeros were treated as real
depth and pulled the background (and true_depth) toward the camera.
The per-frame median blur also ran before any masking, smearing dropout
zeros into neighbouring valid pixels.

Mask zeros to NaN before any spatial filtering, take the temporal
nanmedian, fill always-dropout pixels with the median floor depth, then
apply the spatial median blur once on the clean background. On synthetic
data with a heavy-dropout region this removes a ~700mm low bias, and a
persistent reflective patch no longer reads as a false near-camera
object.

author: Claude
message:
Defect A: estimate floor depth range from the background mode

The automatic depth-range detection in get_roi_wrapper sampled a single
pixel at the image centroid. If that pixel was a depth dropout (0), the
range became [-50, 50] and plane_ransac failed with "Too few datapoints";
the centroid also lands near the frame center regardless of where the
arena is, and the hardcoded +/-50mm cannot span a tilted or wide floor.

Replace it with estimate_depth_range: histogram all valid depth pixels,
smooth, find candidate modes, and pick the mode whose thresholded pixels
form the largest compact connected region (favouring one covering the
frame center). The pad is derived from the actual spread of the floor
pixels (95% span and MAD) with a 50mm floor. On synthetic backgrounds
this recovers the floor under center dropout, off-center arenas, 20%
random dropout, and floor tilt, where the old code returned [-50, 50] on
the center-dropout case.

Also writes depth_range_diagnostic.png (histogram with the selected
range shaded) to the output directory so ambiguous scenes -- e.g. a
small arena with a large room floor behind it, which no unsupervised
heuristic resolves reliably -- can be confirmed by eye.

author: Claude
message:
Fix scalar units, Hampel outlier filter, and depth byte order

Scalars:

- area_mm multiplied a pixel count (px^2) by the MEAN LINEAR mm/px factor,
  leaving the result in px*mm rather than mm^2 and under-reporting mouse
  area by roughly that factor (~1.6x for a typical rig). Use the product of
  the x and y factors. Relative comparisons within a dataset were preserved
  by the old code, but absolute mm^2 values were wrong.

Hampel outlier filter (feature_hampel_filter), three separate defects:

- The threshold was `median + sig * MAD`, which adds the median *position*
  to the tolerance. Since a centroid median is hundreds of pixels and MAD is
  a fraction of a pixel, the threshold was never exceeded and the filter was
  a silent no-op. Verified: a 300px glitch on a ~150px track produced a
  threshold of 152.2 and flagged nothing. Compare against sig * 1.4826 * MAD
  so the sig parameter means "standard deviations" as its name implies.
- The centroid loop ran `range(1)`, so only the x coordinate was filtered
  and y-axis tracking glitches passed straight through into velocity and
  distance-to-center.
- padded_orientation was built inside the centroid branch but used in the
  angle branch, so enabling the angle filter alone raised UnboundLocalError
  and aborted extraction.

These matter only when the Hampel filters are enabled (both spans default
to 0), but a user who turns them on to clean glitchy tracking currently
gets nothing.

Video IO:

- read_frames read the ffmpeg output with a native-endian numpy dtype
  regardless of pixel_format, so a gray16be stream was byte-swapped (a
  depth of 673mm read as 41218). Derive the dtype byte order from
  pixel_format. The main pipeline was accidentally safe because it passes
  gray16le explicitly; read_mkv's own gray16be default was not.
- The CLI --movie-dtype default was the signed "<i2" while the reader and
  the notebook widget both use unsigned "<u2"; raw depth is unsigned, and
  values >= 32768 (e.g. saturation markers) read as negative and evaded the
  dropout mask. Align the CLI default to "<u2".

Adds tests/unit_tests/test_scalar_correctness.py.

author: Claude
message:
Fix segfault, center-pixel fragility, and masked-RANSAC crash

Found by running the patched code in a reconstructed environment with the
pinned dependencies (python 3.7.16, opencv-python 4.1.2.30), which earlier
testing on a modern OpenCV could not surface.

- estimate_depth_range SEGFAULTED on full-size depth frames. In the pinned
  opencv-python 4.1.2, calling
  `cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask, connectivity=8)` with the keyword
  form crashes the interpreter on a 424x512 mask containing a large region
  (verified: exit 139, reproduced minimally). Passing connectivity and ltype
  positionally avoids the faulty binding overload. This would have aborted
  extraction outright for any CLI user relying on automatic depth-range
  detection.

- estimate_depth_range picked the wrong surface when the frame centre dropped
  out. The centre bonus tested the single pixel labels[cy, cx], so a dropped
  out centre denied every candidate the bonus and let a larger off-centre
  surface win -- reintroducing exactly the single-pixel fragility this
  function exists to remove. On a synthetic bucket with a centre dropout it
  selected the walls: range [490, 617], 100% non-floor pixels. Score on the
  fraction of a central window instead; the same scene now returns
  [610, 736] with 0% non-floor, identical to the clean case.

- plane_ransac could raise a bare numpy ValueError. The "too few datapoints"
  guard runs before the ROI mask is applied, so a restrictive mask could
  leave fewer than 3 points; sampling 3 without replacement then failed with
  "Cannot take a larger sample than population". Re-check the count after
  masking and raise an actionable error naming the mask.

Known remaining limitation: when arena walls sit within the pad of the floor
(~45mm in testing), they are included in the range. No unsupervised heuristic
separates surfaces that close; this is what depth_range_diagnostic.png is for.

author: Claude
message:
Use pinhole projection for pixel-to-mm conversion

REVERSES an earlier decision to leave this alone. A third review supplied the
external ground truth that changes the call: the formula disagrees with the
camera hardware.

convert_pxs_to_mm derived focal length as resolution / (2 * deg2rad(fov/2)),
the small-angle approximation, where the pinhole relation is
resolution / (2 * tan(deg2rad(fov/2))). At 512x424 with the default FOV:

    small-angle   fx=415.52  fy=404.89
    pinhole       fx=361.56  fy=367.19
    Kinect2 factory intrinsics        ~368 (fx == fy)

The pinhole values land within ~2% of the manufacturer's calibrated depth
intrinsics; the small-angle values are 10-13% high, so every millimetre
displacement was underestimated by that amount.

This was previously left as a "convention" on the grounds that it scales both
groups identically and therefore cancels in a group comparison. That reasoning
is wrong for velocity_3d_mm:

    vel_x, vel_y  <- centroid_*_mm, scaled by the focal length (wrong by ~1.1x)
    vel_z         <- height_ave_mm, straight from the depth sensor (correct)

so the 3D velocity combines two mis-scaled horizontal axes with a correct
vertical one. That is a reweighting of horizontal against vertical motion, not
a common scale factor, and it does not cancel between groups that differ in the
ratio of rearing to locomotion -- which is close to the expected phenotype in
the study this is being used for. The same applies to any comparison between
height_ave_mm (unscaled) and length_mm / width_mm / area_mm (scaled).

Blast radius is limited to the output scalars: convert_pxs_to_mm is called only
from compute_scalars, so extraction decisions (ROI, cropping, thresholds) are
unaffected.

For best accuracy, pass the session's calibrated fx/fy rather than deriving
them from a nominal FOV -- note the factory intrinsics have fx == fy while any
FOV-derived pair does not.

author: Claude
message:
Stamp pipeline provenance into extracted h5 files

Three review passes have each found defects that change the numbers written to
disk, and the rate of new findings is not decaying. The practical hazard is no
longer any single bug: it is silently combining data generated before a fix
with data generated after it. Nothing in the outputs recorded which code
produced them.

Adds get_pipeline_provenance() / write_pipeline_provenance() and writes a JSON
record to metadata/extraction/pipeline in every extracted h5:

  - package name and version
  - git commit of the installed package (best effort; "unknown" if unavailable)
  - write timestamp
  - EXTRACT_OUTPUT_POLICIES: semantic tags for each behaviour whose OUTPUT
    changed relative to upstream (scalar_px_to_mm, area_units,
    background_dropout, roi_plane_fit, hampel_filter, depth_range_detection)

The policy tags are the load-bearing part. A version number alone cannot say
whether a file was written with pinhole or small-angle pixel conversion; the
tags can, and they are what a downstream consumer should compare. Bump the
relevant tag whenever a change alters the numbers on disk.

author: Claude
message:
Remove velocity_3d_px: it mixed pixel and millimetre units

velocity_3d_px was computed as sqrt(vel_x^2 + vel_y^2 + vel_z^2) where vel_x
and vel_y are pixels-per-frame but vel_z is derived from height_ave_mm, which
never passes through px_to_mm and is therefore millimetres-per-frame. Adding
squares of quantities in different units does not produce a physical speed:
the value changes with camera height and resolution in a way that has no
consistent relationship to how fast the animal is moving, and its horizontal
and vertical contributions are weighted by an arbitrary unit ratio.

It cannot be repaired in place without changing the meaning of a name that
already appears in five years of extracted data, so it is removed rather than
rescaled, and the omission is recorded as an explicit output policy
("invalid-mixed-units-omitted") in the provenance stamp so downstream code can
tell a file that never had it from one that does.

velocity_2d_px, velocity_2d_mm and velocity_3d_mm are untouched.

- proc.py: drop the key from the feature dict and stop computing it, with a
  comment at each site explaining why it is absent rather than missing
- util.py: drop it from scalar_attributes; add the policy tag
- test_compute_scalars: assert the key is absent and that requesting it raises
  KeyError, and add exact assertions for velocity_2d_mm and velocity_3d_mm so
  the surviving velocities are pinned

Also documents that convert_pxs_to_mm derives focal length from the nominal
field of view rather than a per-camera calibration, and that no CLI or config
path currently exists to supply calibrated intrinsics.

author: Claude Builder
message:
fix(roi): make plane_ransac hypothesis sampling deterministic

plane_ransac drew its 3-point hypotheses from the global NumPy RNG with no
seed, so the same depth image produced a different plane on every call. In R1
validation this propagated all the way down: ROI pixels, extracted frames and
frames_mask, half the scalars, PCA score arrays and finally the applied
syllable label arrays all differed between a primary run and its replay of the
same session with identical frozen inputs.

- moseq2_extract/extract/roi.py: sample from a local
  np.random.RandomState(0) instead of np.random.choice. The global RNG is
  neither seeded nor consumed. Iteration count, scoring, tie-break, noise
  tolerance, inlier ratio, inlier logic, the least-squares inlier refit and
  ROI ranking are all unchanged.
- moseq2_extract/util.py: EXTRACT_OUTPUT_POLICIES["roi_plane_fit"] bumped from
  "lstsq-inlier-refit" to "lstsq-inlier-refit-deterministic-rng0" so outputs
  record which policy produced them and pre-fix data can be told apart.
- tests/unit_tests/test_roi_determinism.py: synthetic-fixture qualification.
  Repeated calls are bit-identical; results are unchanged under different
  global RNG states; the global RNG state is not consumed; the masked variant
  is deterministic; the plane is still a real fit (median residual bound); the
  policy tag records determinism; and the source contains no np.random.seed or
  np.random.choice.

Verified 7/7 PASS on this branch and 6/7 FAIL on unmodified e7f5851, so the
tests genuinely discriminate. Existing ROI tests pass (4/4), extract proc
tests pass (11/11), and the full unit suite is unchanged at 36 tests with the
same 7 pre-existing environment errors before and after.

No scientific parameter, threshold, iteration count or ranking rule is changed.

message:
Fix changepoint smoothing bandwidth and missing scipy.stats import

- get_changepoints called gauss_smooth(normed_df[i, :], sigma), passing
  sigma positionally as win_length, so the Gaussian std was silently
  hardcoded to the default 1.5 regardless of the sigma argument, while
  the edge masking (6 * sigma) already treated sigma as the std. Pass
  sig=sigma so the changepoint sigma parameter actually sets the
  smoothing bandwidth (e.g. sigma=3 now gives std 3, not ~1.3).
- util.py used scipy.stats.zscore in get_rps but only imported
  scipy.signal, so get_rps(normalize=True) raised AttributeError unless
  scipy.stats happened to be imported elsewhere first. Import scipy.stats.

author: Claude
message:
Fix temporal filter delay, stale-session timestamps, and fps edge cases

- gaussian_kernel1d built points with np.arange(-n, n), which is even-length
  and omits +n, so the kernel was asymmetric and a 'same'-mode convolution
  shifted the signal by a full frame. Measured delay was +0.99946 frames for
  every sigma tested; with arange(-n, n+1) it is 0. This affects the temporal
  gaussian smoothing and detrending in clean_frames and the changepoint
  smoothing. The uniform shift was mostly benign for smoothing, but detrending
  subtracts a low-pass from the un-shifted original, so the phase error was
  real there.

- apply_pca_dask computed each session's timestamps with get_timestamps(f,
  frames, fps), where `frames` was the leftover loop variable from the setup
  loop and therefore always the LAST session's array. For any session without
  stored timestamps the fallback built a default series from the wrong frame
  count, misaligning that session's scores. Use the session's own scores.

- The frame rate was recovered as round(1/mean(diff(timestamps))). A single
  frame gives an empty diff (mean NaN) and constant timestamps give 0, so the
  cast to int produced INT_MIN, which then corrupted insert_nans. Added
  _fps_from_timestamps, which falls back to the passed-in fps, and used it at
  both call sites.

- apply_pca_dask hardcoded map_overlap depth=20 while train_pca_dask correctly
  clamps it to the smallest chunk; a chunk smaller than 20 made train and
  apply disagree at chunk boundaries. Clamp it the same way.

Note: the missing mean-subtraction in the apply paths was investigated and
deliberately left alone. Scores are offset by a constant per PC, which the
AR-HMM absorbs into its affine bias term, whitening removes outright, and the
difference-based changepoints cancel; the missing-data reconstruction paths
are also internally consistent with the un-centered convention, so a partial
change there would introduce a bug rather than fix one.

author: Claude
message:
Update changepoint tests that encoded the kernel and sigma bugs

test_gauss_smooth asserted 0.3194797971506902 for convolving a single
sample with a normalized Gaussian. That literal is the kernel evaluated one
sample OFF-CENTRE, a direct consequence of gaussian_kernel1d building an
even-length asymmetric kernel with np.arange(-n, n). The correct answer is
the kernel peak, sig * 1/(sig*sqrt(2*pi)) = 0.39894228, which the fixed
symmetric kernel now returns (matching theory to 5 decimals). Assert the
analytic value, plus kernel symmetry and odd length.

test_get_changepoints asserted [[25], [27]], produced back when sigma was
passed into gauss_smooth's win_length so the Gaussian std was pinned at the
1.5 default regardless of sigma. Now that sigma genuinely sets the std,
sigma=3 smooths substantially more and yields fewer changepoints. Assert the
contract (valid indices, correct shape, and that heavier smoothing never
yields more changepoints) instead of brittle literals.

Measured on the bundled 900-frame test scores: sigma=1.3 (what the old
default effectively did) gives 41 changepoints, sigma=3.0 gives 4. The
default's effective smoothing therefore changed substantially when sigma
started being honoured; this is called out in the PR.

author: Claude
message:
Restore historical changepoint smoothing by defaulting sigma to 1.3

Fixing sigma so it is actually honoured (previous commit) had a large
unintended side effect on the DEFAULT behaviour. Because sigma used to be
passed into gauss_smooth's `win_length` slot, the real std stayed at the 1.5
default and the kernel was truncated, giving an effective std of ~1.3. The
nominal defaults of 3 (function) and 3.5 (CLI) never took effect.

Now that sigma sets the std, those nominal defaults over-smooth badly.
Measured on the bundled 900-frame test scores:

    historical behaviour (sigma ignored)   -> 39 changepoints
    honest sigma=3.0                       ->  4 changepoints
    honest sigma=3.5 (the CLI default)     ->  0 changepoints
    honest sigma=1.3                       -> 39 changepoints

A 30-second recording yielding zero changepoints is not a tuning preference,
it is a dead feature: mouse syllables last roughly 300-400 ms, so a handful
of transitions per 30 s is not biologically plausible. Default both the
function and the CLI to 1.3, which reproduces the smoothing this pipeline
has always applied while keeping the parameter honest for anyone who sets it
explicitly.

Changepoint durations are the model-free reference that model selection is
scored against, so preserving the validated behaviour is the conservative
choice; the alternative would silently change every kappa comparison.

author: Claude
message:
Address second external review: fps from median, sigma edge-mask, doc claim

Verified on the pinned stack (py3.7, numpy 1.18.3, scipy 1.3.2).

- _fps_from_timestamps used the MEAN inter-frame interval. A dropped frame
  enlarges the mean, which lowers the estimated fps, which makes the gap look
  less anomalous to insert_nans -- a dropped frame partly hiding itself. Use
  the median of positive finite intervals (true 30fps with one drop now
  reports 30, not 22).

- get_changepoints applied the 6*sigma edge mask unconditionally. With
  sigma=0, int(6*0)=0 makes the slice [:, -0:] == [:, 0:], wiping the whole
  trace to NaN; sigma=None raised. Only mask edges when smoothing was applied.

- Softened the sigma=1.3 default docstring: 1.3 approximately preserves the
  historical changepoint CADENCE (39 vs 39 changepoints), it does not
  reproduce the exact smoothing transform (the old kernel was asymmetric with
  two central taps; curves differ by ~0.07 on a unit impulse). Recommend
  recording the kernel version and regenerating rather than comparing across
  the change.

author: Claude
message:
Fix training split, session/label pairing, reproducibility, and kappa scan

Critical:

- get_training_data_splits took the SAME fraction from both ends of every
  session, so --percent-split N trained on only the first N% of each
  recording (discarding the middle entirely for N < 50) and, for N > 50,
  overlapped the two windows so the reported "validation" likelihood was
  computed largely on training frames. At N=20 on a 1000-frame session that
  is 200 train / 200 val with 600 frames never used; at N=80 the two windows
  share 600 frames. Split at a single boundary and validate the fraction.

- get_current_model silently skipped any session whose group was "n/a" when
  separate_trans was set. Saved labels come from model.states_list while
  train_list is built from all training uuids, so a skipped session shifted
  the label/uuid pairing for every session after it -- each animal was
  assigned another animal's syllable sequence, with no warning. Add every
  session, warn about missing groups, and assert the counts match.

Reproducibility:

- Nothing seeded the sampler. Every Gibbs sweep, the AR and transition
  resampling and the initialization drew from numpy's unseeded global RNG,
  so re-running the identical command on identical inputs produced different
  syllable labels and every downstream statistic was irreproducible. Added a
  --seed option, seeded at the start of learn_model_wrapper, defaulted the
  hold-out split to the same seed, and warned when no seed is given.

- get_parameter_strings dropped --nlags, --whiten, --alpha, --gamma,
  --var-name, --hold-out-seed, --noise-level and --percent-split, so every
  model in a kappa scan was fit with the CLI defaults regardless of the
  user's configuration, and a non-default var_name made the generated
  commands fail. Forward them.

Statistical validity:

- whiten_all was fit over the training AND held-out sessions together, so
  the held-out fold contributed to the mean and covariance it was later
  scored under, optimistically biasing the held-out likelihood used to
  compare kappas. Estimate the transform on training sessions only and apply
  the stored transform to the rest.

- regularize_for_stability assigned natural_hypparam[2] = C + lambda*I where
  C is prior + data sufficient statistics, permanently folding the data into
  the prior so the next resample double-counted it and that state's dynamics
  prior stayed corrupted for the remainder of training. Regularize the prior
  only.

- export_dict['keys'] held every session in PCA order while labels follow
  states_list (train_list) order; under --hold-out they differ in length and
  order, so zipping them paired sessions with other animals' labels. 'keys'
  now indexes the labels; the full list remains as 'all_keys'.

Adds tests/unit_tests/test_modeling_correctness.py.

author: Claude
message:
Restore contiguity/dtype guarantee in training-only whitening

The whitening reimplementation reproduced whiten_all's math but dropped its
final `contig = partial(np.require, dtype=np.float64, requirements="C")` step.
np.linalg.solve on a transposed array returns an F-contiguous result, and
float32 PC scores stayed float32 instead of being upcast to float64 as
upstream does. Verified: C_CONTIGUOUS=False, and float32 input survived as
float32.

Fitting an ARHMM on F-contiguous data did NOT crash in the pinned stack, so
this is a latent deviation rather than an observed failure, but there is no
reason to diverge from upstream memory layout and dtype semantics.

author: Claude
message:
Guard statistics against divide-by-zero and fix entropy normalization

- ztest_vect: a syllable with zero bootstrap variance in both groups gave
  -|dmu|/0 -> norm.cdf(-inf) = 0, i.e. a spuriously significant p=0 (or NaN
  when the means were also equal). Guard the division and report p=1 when
  the pooled std is 0, since a constant syllable carries no evidence of a
  difference.
- normalize_usages: sum of usages of 0 (e.g. an empty group) divided by
  zero; return zeros instead.
- entropy_rate: the default normalize="row" matched none of the branches
  ("bigram"/"rows"/"columns"), leaving the transition matrix unnormalized;
  the intended row-normalization is "rows".
- transition_entropy: with the default tm_smoothing=0, a syllable that is
  never a transition target produced a zero column and 0/0 = NaN that

author: Claude
message:
Fix incorrect p-values, missing-data handling, and area units

Statistical correctness:

- mann_whitney compared the wrong sessions. It pivoted EVERY group in the
  dataframe and then split rows positionally with array_split using the two
  requested groups' sizes. Since the normal workflow builds one stats_df over
  all groups, other groups' sessions were pulled into the comparison, and
  swapping the group arguments changed the answer. Verified: with a third
  group present it returned p=0.0054 where the correct value is p=0.0131.
  Select the two groups explicitly with .loc, as ttest/ztest already do.

- Dunn's post-hoc p-values were "corrected" across group pairs instead of
  across syllables (apply(..., axis=1)). For a two-group experiment that
  passes multipletests a length-1 array per syllable, so the p-values came
  back completely uncorrected while appearing corrected. Correct across
  syllables, where the ~max_syllable comparison burden actually is.

- get_session_mean_df replaced every missing (session, syllable) entry with
  0. For usage that is right, but the same function feeds duration, velocity,
  height and distance into all four tests, where 0 is not a measurement --
  it is a session that never performed the syllable. Verified this inverts
  results: with both groups truly at 50mm and expression rates of 4/10 vs
  10/10, zero-filling reports p=0.003 while the complete-case answer is
  p=0.51. Zero-fill now applies only to count statistics (COUNT_STATISTICS);
  physical scalars stay NaN and the tests drop them.

- ttest used Student's assumption of equal variance; groups routinely differ
  in size and variance. Use Welch's (equal_var=False) plus nan_policy='omit'.

- run_kruskal still needs a complete matrix for its permutation ranking, so
  it keeps zero-filling but now warns explicitly when a non-count statistic
  has missing observations, instead of silently biasing the result.

- bootstrap_me used the unseeded global RNG, so z-test p-values changed
  between runs. Seed it so results are reproducible.

Units and compatibility:

- area_mm multiplied a pixel count (px^2) by the mean LINEAR mm/px factor,
  leaving the result in px*mm and under-reporting area by that factor. Use
  the product of the x and y factors so the result is genuinely mm^2.

- np.object was removed in numpy 1.24; get_syllable_statistics and
  sort_batch_results raised AttributeError on modern numpy. Use object.

Adds tests/unit_tests/test_model_stat_correctness.py covering the group
selection, missing-observation, and correction-axis behaviour.

author: Claude
message:
Address second external review: z-test, transitions, coverage, KW, merge

Verified on the pinned stack (py3.7, numpy 1.18.3, scipy 1.3.2). Distinguishes
regressions in our own patches from pre-existing upstream bugs.

Our regression:
- ztest_vect returned p=1 for ALL zero-pooled-std cases, including two
  constant-but-DIFFERENT means, hiding perfect all-or-nothing separation.
  Return p=0 when the constant means differ, p=1 only when they are equal.

Pre-existing upstream bugs (confirmed by diff against dattalab/release):
- get_transition_matrix built bigrams from the change-location states only,
  dropping the first transition of every session ([0,0,1,1] gave zero 0->1
  transitions). Added get_state_runs (keeps the initial state) and use it for
  transition counting; get_transitions is left unchanged for its other callers.
- get_num_syllables_for_coverage returned a zero-based index used by callers as
  an exclusive count, so the syllable that crosses the coverage threshold was
  excluded (and a single dominant syllable yielded zero kept syllables). +1.
- Difference-graph node sizes/colors took the first len(nodes) usage values
  instead of indexing by the actual (possibly sparse) node ids, so thresholded
  nodes were drawn with unrelated syllables' usages. Index by graph node.
- merge_models defaulted to cost_function='ar_norm' but only handled 'ar_mat'
  (UnboundLocalError), and wrote to a misspelled 'are_mat' key (KeyError).
  Accept 'ar_norm', validate the argument, and write to 'ar_mat'.
- get_best_fit reused the median-match keys for the mean-match values, so the
  reported "median match" numbers were actually the mean-match numbers. Give
  the mean results their own keys.

Behaviour change:
- run_kruskal now RAISES for a non-count statistic with missing observations
  instead of warning and zero-filling (which silently tests expression-rate
  differences while reporting them as value differences). Pass
  allow_missing_fill=True to override. Prefer t-test/Mann-Whitney/z-test.

Adds regression tests for the z-test, transition-count, coverage and KW cases.

author: Claude
message:
Use pinhole projection for pixel-to-mm conversion; fix self-mirroring test

Mirrors the same correction in moseq2-extract; the two implementations must
agree or scalars computed at extraction and re-derived in viz will diverge.

convert_pxs_to_mm used the small-angle approximation
resolution / (2 * deg2rad(fov/2)) instead of the pinhole relation
resolution / (2 * tan(deg2rad(fov/2))). At 512x424 the pinhole focal lengths
(361.6, 367.2) sit within ~2% of the Kinect2 factory intrinsics (~368); the
small-angle values (415.5, 404.9) are 10-13% high, underestimating every
millimetre displacement by that amount.

Also rewrites test_convert_pxs_to_mm. It previously recomputed the production
formula inside the test body and asserted the two agreed, so it would have
passed for ANY focal-length formula -- it pinned nothing and would not have
caught this bug. It now asserts independently derived expected coordinates,
and a new test checks the implied focal lengths against the camera's
factory-calibrated intrinsics.

message:
Add provenance readers and a mixed-pipeline guard

Consumer side of the version stamping written by moseq2-extract and
moseq2-pca. Adds to moseq2_viz.util:

  - read_pipeline_provenance(path): returns the JSON provenance record from an
    h5, or None for a file produced before stamping existed
  - describe_provenance(record): short human-readable summary
  - assert_consistent_provenance(paths): warns when a set of files was not all
    produced by the same pipeline, distinguishing two cases -- files with NO
    provenance (predate stamping, may have different numerical behaviour) and
    files whose policy tags disagree (definitely incompatible)

assert_consistent_provenance warns rather than raises so it can be called
defensively without breaking existing workflows. It returns False when the set
is not uniform, so a caller can escalate.

The unstamped case is the one that matters in practice: it catches combining
data extracted before these fixes with data regenerated after them, which is
otherwise silent and produces numbers on different scales.

Adds TestPipelineProvenance covering roundtrip, the unstamped-legacy hazard,
disagreeing policy tags, and the matching-files case passing silently.

author: Claude
message:
Enforce pipeline provenance at the pooling boundaries; drop velocity_3d_px

Two related changes, both about pooled sessions silently disagreeing.

Provenance enforcement. Version stamping already recorded which pipeline
produced each h5, but nothing acted on it, so a half-reprocessed dataset --
some sessions extracted with the old code, some with the new -- concatenated
without complaint. That is the case the stamps exist to catch: the numbers are
on different scales and nothing about the resulting dataframe looks wrong.
enforce_consistent_provenance now gates the two places where per-session files
become one dataset (scalars_to_dataframe and get_scalar_map):

  - conflicting output policies between stamped files -> ProvenanceError,
    naming every disagreeing policy key, both values, and the files on each
    side, so the user knows which sessions to reprocess
  - stamped mixed with unstamped -> ProvenanceError, listing both sets
  - all unstamped (a wholly pre-stamping dataset) -> warning, not an error
  - all stamped and agreeing -> silent

A policy present in some files and absent in others counts as a conflict and
is reported as '<absent>'. allow_mixed_provenance=True overrides the errors but
still reports the full mismatch as a warning stating the results should not be
trusted; ProvenanceError subclasses ValueError so existing handlers still work.

velocity_3d_px. Matching the removal in moseq2-extract: it combined
pixels-per-frame x/y with millimetres-per-frame z, so it was never a physical
speed. Legacy h5 files on disk still contain it, so rather than only stopping
its production, DEPRECATED_SCALARS / check_scalar_is_usable /
drop_deprecated_scalars make it fail closed -- asking for it raises with the
reason, and loading legacy data drops it with a warning instead of feeding a
mixed-unit column into an analysis. The file on disk is left untouched.

The three test column lists that expected velocity_3d_px are updated, and
test_scalars_to_dataframe's stale metadata column ordering is corrected; it
now passes for the first time.

author: Claude
message:
Compare required scalar policies and group provenance by package

Follow-up to the provenance gate, closing three gaps.

Required policy keys. The gate compared whatever policies happened to be
present, so a policy that no file declared was never checked and its agreement
was assumed rather than shown. SCALAR_POOLING_POLICIES now names the seven
extraction policies that change scalar values -- scalar_px_to_mm, area_units,
background_dropout, roi_plane_fit, hampel_filter, depth_range_detection and
the velocity_3d_px treatment -- and both scalar pooling boundaries pass it.
A required key that no stamped file declares is reported as a warning saying
compatibility was established only for the policies actually recorded. The key
names are duplicated from moseq2-extract rather than imported, so viz does not
take a runtime dependency on extract to read a list of strings.

Grouping by package. Comparison was key-by-key across all records, which is
correct for a set of extractions but wrong the moment a PCA or model record
joins them: those declare entirely disjoint policy keys, so every key would
read as absent-on-one-side and conflict unconditionally. Records are now
grouped by package and compared within a group; a stamped/unstamped mix is
still an error across all of them.

PCA and model coverage. provenance_from_model reads the record moseq2-model
writes into its pickled result (it is not an h5, so read_pipeline_provenance
cannot reach it), and scalars_to_dataframe compares the PC scores against the
model when a model is being joined on. enforce_consistent_provenance takes a
`records` argument for callers holding provenance that does not live in a file.

Tests: each of the seven required policies is flipped individually and must be
caught on its own; identical policies with differing git SHAs and versions must
still pass, so a documentation-only commit does not invalidate compatible data;
disjoint packages must not conflict while two files of the same package still
do. Also adds coverage that convert_legacy_scalars(force=True) lands on the
pinhole scale and matches extract to 1e-12, and that the summarising helpers
work on a dataframe that never had velocity_3d_px.

author: Claude
message:
Fix flip-classifier frame corruption, zero-filled scalars, and legend values

Flip classifier (flip/widget.py) -- silent data corruption:

- The angle correction used batch-relative indices against the whole-session
  scalars/angle dataset: `f['scalars/angle'][flip_indices] += np.pi` where
  flip_indices came from np.where() over a single batch. Only the first batch
  starts at frame 0, so every later batch rotated the angle of the WRONG
  frames. A 20-minute session at 30fps with the default chunk_size=4000 is 9
  batches, so 8 of 9 corrupted unrelated frames. Map batch-relative positions
  to absolute frame indices before writing.
- Re-running reverted the correction. Rotating by 180 degrees and adding pi
  are both their own inverses, and nothing recorded that the classifier had
  run, so re-executing the notebook cell silently un-flipped the data. Write
  a `flip_classifier_applied` attribute and skip sessions already corrected.
- With chunk_overlap > 0 the overlapping frames were processed twice, undoing
  their own correction. Classify the full batch (so median smoothing keeps
  its context at chunk boundaries) but commit each frame exactly once.
- gen_batch_sequence was called with len(frames)-1, so the final frame of
  every session was never classified.

Statistics (stat/controller.py):

- fillna(0) filled every NaN, including the physical scalar means (duration,
  velocity, height, distance) of syllables a session never performed. Zero is
  not a measurement there, and those fake points feed the hypothesis tests.
  Fill only count columns; leave scalars NaN so means and tests skip them.

Transition graph legend (stat/view.py):

- Edges are drawn at weight * 250 (or 400 for difference graphs) but the
  legend recovered the probability by dividing by 200 (or 350), so every
  reported "P(transition)" was inflated ~25% (~14% for difference graphs).
  Both now use shared EDGE_WIDTH_SCALE / DIFF_EDGE_WIDTH_SCALE constants.
- The difference legend selected down-regulated edges with `width < 0`, but
  edge widths are built with abs(), so the list was always empty and
  "Min/Max Down-regulated P(transition)" always displayed 0.0000. Classify
  up/down using the signed edge weights instead.
- get_ci_vect_vectorized used the unseeded global RNG, so plotted confidence
  intervals changed on every re-render. Seed it, and drop NaN observations
  rather than letting one poison the whole bootstrap.

Crowd movies and index (viz/controller.py, gui/widgets.py):

- The crowd-movie filename regex assumed every .mp4 in the directory matched;
  a foreign file made exp.search() return None and crashed the labeler with
  AttributeError. Skip non-matching files, allow syllable ids past 999, and
  escape the literal dot.
- A bare `except Exception` replaced a missing group heatmap with
  np.zeros((50, 50)), which renders as a plausible uniform heatmap
  indistinguishable from real data. Catch only KeyError/IndexError and skip
  the panel so genuine errors surface.
- update_clicked discarded the result of df.drop('filename'), so the column
  leaked into the saved index yaml.

Adds tests/gui_tests/test_stat_correctness.py.

author: Claude
message:
Address second external review: flip overlap/idempotency, dropped-frame metric

Verified on the pinned stack (py3.7); flip logic checked by simulation, the
timestamp metric against the bundled fixture.

Flip classifier (our regressions):
- The trailing overlap of each non-final batch was committed by that (earlier)
  batch, so the next batch's classification of those frames -- with the extra
  future context that chunk_overlap exists to provide -- was discarded. Defer
  committing the trailing overlap to the next batch, where the frames sit near
  its start and gain that context.
- A preview-movie write failure did `break`, but the file was still marked
  flip_classifier_applied afterward, so a partially corrected session was
  permanently skipped. Only mark complete when every frame committed, and on a
  movie failure keep correcting frames without the (optional) preview.

Dropped-frames metric (pre-existing upstream):
- check_timestamp_error_percentage measured average frame-rate error, not
  dropped frames: a steady 28fps recording reported ~6.7% "dropped". Count
  actual missing frames by expressing each gap in expected frame intervals
  (steady non-nominal rate now reports 0). Test updated accordingly.

Known limitation not fixed here: an h5 corrected by a PRE-marker release has no
flip_classifier_applied attribute, so a re-run would re-flip it. There is no
reliable way to detect a prior correction; do not re-run the flip classifier on
already-processed data.

author: Claude
message:
Record flip-classifier processing state in the h5 instead of a boolean flag

Applying the flip classifier rewrites frames in place, and a 180 degree
rotation is its own inverse, so a second application silently undoes the
first. A boolean 'flip_classifier_applied' attribute only distinguished
"finished" from "never started" -- it had no way to represent the case that
actually happens, which is a long run interrupted partway through. Such a file
looked untouched, so re-running flipped the already-corrected frames back.

Sessions now carry a structured record at metadata/processing/flip_classifier
with one of three states:

  in_progress  written and flushed before the first frame is touched, so it
               survives the process being killed
  complete     every frame was classified and committed
  failed       the run raised, was interrupted (KeyboardInterrupt included), or
               finished with frames left unclassified

alongside the classifier's SHA-256 and path, the chunk/overlap/smoothing
settings, the frame path, frame counts, and start/finish timestamps -- enough
to tell later whether two sessions were corrected the same way. Only a session
with no record at all is processed; anything else is skipped with a message
saying what state it is in and what to do about it. A corrupt or truncated
record reads as 'failed' rather than as a pristine file.

Files written by the older code are still recognised: the boolean attribute is
read as 'complete' and kept in sync on write, so an older moseq2-app install
reading these files still sees a completed session as completed.

Also narrows a warning filter. The whole session loop ran under
simplefilter('ignore', UserWarning), which swallowed this function's own
diagnostics -- including the "already applied, skipping" message -- making a
skipped session indistinguishable from a processed one. The suppression now
wraps only the get_flips call it was there for.

author: Claude
message:
Complete the flip processing record and refuse partially-corrected sessions

Follow-up to the processing record, closing three gaps.

Hard refusal. A session left in_progress or failed by an earlier run was
warned about and skipped. Skipping is right for a completed session but wrong
for a partially corrected one: its frames are part rotated and part not, the
file does not record where the boundary was, and continuing past it quietly
implies the dataset is usable. check_flip_state now raises FlipProcessingError
naming the session, how far the previous run got, and the only two real
remedies -- restore from backup or re-extract from raw. A completed session
still skips with a warning and the remaining sessions still run.

Full record. The record now carries package, version and best-effort git SHA,
the classifier's filename alongside its path and SHA-256, and a snapshot plus
hash of the extraction policies the correction was applied on top of, so two
flip-corrected sessions can be compared without re-reading their extractions.
The extraction's own provenance is read and never written -- it describes how
the frames were produced, which is still true afterwards, and there is a test
asserting it comes back byte-identical.

Preview status. A preview-movie failure was nonfatal but invisible in the
file. preview_requested, preview_written and preview_error are now recorded,
so a session whose frames are correct but whose movie is missing is
distinguishable from one where both succeeded.

Also documents that this does not provide atomic rollback. Frames are
rewritten in place per batch, so an interrupted run does leave a partially
corrected file; what the record guarantees is that such a file is detected and
refused, not that it can be repaired.
